messages:
maria: quick heads-up — running mixed-quant routing (AWQ primary, GPTQ fallback) on canary and seeing weird prefix-cache behaviour. hit rate dropped ~12% and tail latency spiked on some shards. anyone else?

sanjay: yep saw that in my local canary yesterday. looked like the cache key collisions between quant variants. hit-rate before: 0.87, after: 0.76.

derek: interesting. what config for continuous batching + prefetch? we recently set `batch.max_wait_ms=8` and `prefetch.enabled=true` on the canary pool.

maria: exactly that. prefetch TTL is 10s, cache namespace is `kv:v1` (no model-quant tag). routing policy toggles between `awq-1.0` and `gptq-1.3` for capacity fallback.

eva: probable cause: cache keys not including quantization variant -> different output artifacts reuse same prefix cache entry even though KV layout differs across quant backends. leads to corrupted kv cache or forced recompute and miss accounting.

sanjay: reproducer from my run: `./run_infer.sh --model awq-1.0 --batching continuous --prefetch on --key-suffix ''` produced: `kvcache_hit_rate=0.76, avg_p90=120ms, p99=450ms`

derek: good find. quick test idea: namespace the cache by quant tag, e.g. `kv:v1:awq-1.0` vs `kv:v1:gptq-1.3`. worth trying to confirm.

maria: ran that quickly on canary-2 — namespacing + small change in prefetch (TTL 3s) recovered hit-rate to 0.93. numbers: `hit_rate=0.93, avg_p90=98ms, p99=180ms`. no obvious accuracy regression on small eval.

eva: can you share eval delta? on our conversational-1k eval we saw AWQ->GPTQ path had small BLEU/ROUGE deltas last week.

maria: short eval diff after namespacing (AWQ primary, GPTQ fallback): `EM:-0.4, ROUGE-L:-0.6, avg_prob_change:0.002`. baseline (fp16): `EM:0.0, ROUGE-L:0.0` — so small quality cost but much better stability.

sanjay: curious about mixing FP8 too. did you see any bit-compat issues (kernel outputs vary) or just cache semantics?

maria: mostly semantics + different kv-cache encoding across kernels. FP8 produced different prefix bytes so we get more cache churn; when cached under neutral namespace it overwrote previous format and produced invalid hits.

derek: suggests two mitigation strategies: 1) always include model+quant tag in cache key (cheap), 2) do backward-compatible serialization for KV cache (harder). prefer (1) for now.

eva: for rollout, we should also instrument a metric `kvcache_format_mismatch` or track `deserialization_errors` in the runtime to catch silent corruptions.

ops-bot: deploy started: canary 3 -> 3 nodes; change: `kvcache.namespace = kv:v1.${MODEL_QUANT_TAG}` by maria.

maria: small follow-up test results after canary-3: `prefetch=true, prefetch_ttl=3s, namespaced kv` -> `hit_rate=0.94, p90=92ms, p99=170ms`. cost per token down ~6% vs previous fallback-heavy runs.

sanjay: accuracy on full 10k eval (conversational-10k): baseline fp16 vs mixed-quant namespaced: `EM:-0.8, ROUGE-L:-0.9` (still within our regression alert thresholds but notable).

derek: put a regression alert rule: if EM delta <= -1.5 or ROUGE-L <= -1.5 we fail rollout. these numbers are OK for now.

eva: next experiments: test with `batch.max_wait_ms=4` and with `prefetch.enabled=false` to see latency trade-offs. also try a single shared namespace but include a serialization version header in the key (e.g. `kv:v1:v2:awq-1.0`).

maria: I'll run the matrix overnight: dims = [awq/gptq/gptq-int8/fp8], prefetch=[on,off], namespacing=[none,model-quant,model-quant-vtag]. will push results in the morning.

sanjay: ping me if you want help with the eval harness — I have scripts to produce per-example diffs and riser charts.

eva: action items summarized: 1) short-term: namespace kvcache by model+quant (deployed canary), 2) add runtime metric for cache deserialization format mismatches, 3) run full factorial bakeoff (maria), 4) threshold-based rollout gating (derek).

maria: thanks all. will post raw logs + the experiment table in this thread tomorrow. :rocket:
